title: LMM-IR: Large-Scale Netlist-Aware Multimodal Framework for Static IR-Drop Prediction
problem: Static IR drop analysis is a critical bottleneck in chip design, requiring hours of computation per iteration; iterative refinement for violations exacerbates computational burden, making fast prediction essential.
motivation: Reducing IR drop analysis time directly translates to shorter design cycles; machine learning acceleration of this fundamental task can significantly improve design productivity.
method: The approach represents circuit descriptions (SPICE netlists) as 3D point clouds—three-dimensional spatial arrangements—to efficiently handle massive circuits containing hundreds of thousands to millions of connection points. These point cloud representations, combined with circuit images, feed through a large neural network (a machine learning algorithm called a netlist transformer) that learns compact representations from both inputs. A final prediction model combines these learned representations to estimate voltage drop (the unwanted voltage loss that occurs across the circuit).
key_novelty: The innovation is representing circuit structure as 3D point clouds and combining this spatial representation with circuit images in a machine learning system to predict voltage drop on large circuits.
contributions: Netlist transformer encoding circuit topology as scalable 3D point clouds
Multimodal fusion of netlist and image data for IR prediction
